html:
The Pawnee are a Native American people of the central Plains, whose villages stood along the Platte and Loup rivers in what is now Nebraska. They speak a Caddoan language, related to that of the Arikara, the Wichita and the Caddo.

They lived in large villages of earth lodges and farmed maize, beans and squash. Twice a year the whole village left on a bison hunt. Their four bands were the Skidi, Chawi, Kitkahahki and Pitahawirata. The Skidi were known for star lore and a sacred ceremony for the Morning Star.

In 1720 Pawnee and Otoe warriors destroyed a Spanish force from New Mexico in the Villasur expedition, ending Spain's push onto the central Plains. In the 1800s the Pawnee suffered from smallpox and from raids by the Lakota, their great enemies. Pawnee scouts served the US Army. In the 1870s the tribe was moved to Oklahoma, where it is based today.
